title_occupation: ['CRM Automation & RevOps | HubSpot, Pipedrive, GHL, Zoho']
description:
['
You’ve paid for the leads. You’ve paid for the CRM. So why are you still asking the team, “Did anyone actually follow up with this person?”

Someone’s checking a spreadsheet. Someone else thinks an automation handles it. The person who built that automation left six months ago.

Lovely.

I help businesses sort out what happens between someone showing interest and actually becoming a customer. The CRM, the follow-up, the integrations, the reporting. All the things that become painfully important once “we’ll just keep track of it ourselves” stops working.

HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Pipedrive, Zoho. I work across them. Let’s start with what your business needs to do.

🫠 ANY OF THIS SOUND FAMILIAR?

• “We need more leads.”
Possibly. But you’ve also got hundreds of old enquiries sitting in the CRM, no consistent follow-up and no clear idea why people stopped replying. There could be business in there you’ve already paid to acquire.

• “Our sales team won’t use the CRM.”
They’re updating spreadsheets, digging through emails and keeping notes in their heads because that’s somehow easier. Meanwhile, you’re paying for a system that creates more admin for the people it’s supposed to help.

• “We have automations. I think.”
Nobody’s entirely sure what triggers what anymore. A prospect books a call and still gets the “book a call” email. Someone changes a field and three other things break. Everyone’s slightly scared to touch it.

• “Can someone pull the numbers?”
A surprisingly complicated request. Marketing has one answer. Sales has another. You end up piecing together a report manually, then making decisions with a quiet suspicion that half of it is wrong.

• “Why am I still the person holding all this together?”
You’re reminding people to follow up, checking whether leads were assigned and passing information between teams. The business has grown, but far too much still depends on you remembering things.

• “Surely these tools should talk to each other?”
Your forms, calendars, CRM and delivery systems all hold a different piece of the story. Your team fills the gaps by copying and pasting. Sometimes correctly.

🔧 WHAT WE CAN ACTUALLY FIX

📥 Lead handling and follow-up
Get enquiries to the right person, give them a clear next action, and build sensible email, SMS and reminder sequences around the sales process. Including what happens when someone doesn’t book, doesn’t show or isn’t ready yet.

🧩 CRM setup and cleanup
Build pipelines that reflect how you sell, tidy up records and make the system easier to use. That might mean improving what you have, starting fresh or migrating to something that fits better.

🔌 Integrations
Connect the tools your business runs on using Make, Zapier, n8n, webhooks and custom APIs. So your team can stop being the connection between two bits of software.

♻️ Nurture and database reactivation
Give older enquiries a sensible route back into a conversation. “They didn’t buy immediately” shouldn’t be the end of your entire follow-up strategy.

📊 Reporting
See where leads come from, where they get stuck and what turns into sales. Answer everyday business questions without launching a small investigation.

🤖 AI, where it earns its place
Summarise conversations, organise enquiries and help your team get the context they need. There should be a clear reason to add it and a useful job for it to do.

🧠 A BIT ABOUT ME

I’m Johnny. Before running Lock and Quay, I worked in software engineering and business analysis at Deloitte Digital. Since then, I’ve worked across paid ads, lead generation, CRM and marketing automation.

I’ve been on the side spending money to bring leads in. So I care quite a lot about what happens to them afterwards.

That mix shapes how I approach a build. Who’s using this? What do they need to know? What happens if the prospect goes quiet? Who owns the next step? Will this still make sense when there are twice as many enquiries?

I’m also Top Rated Plus on Upwork, with $60K+ earned here and work spanning CRM audits, HubSpot workflows, Pipedrive optimisation and integrations.

🤝 HOW WE’D WORK TOGETHER

Show me what’s happening now and where it’s frustrating you. You don’t need to arrive with a perfect technical brief. Working out what needs building is part of the job.

For a bigger project, we’ll usually start with a paid audit and roadmap. We map the process, identify the gaps and agree on priorities before getting stuck into implementation.

I work best with people who are open about what’s going wrong, happy to answer questions and willing to make decisions together. I’ll bring ideas, flag things that don’t make sense and take ownership of the agreed work.

The goal is a business where leads get handled properly, your team knows what to do and you don’t have to personally chase every moving part.

Send me a message with what you’re using and what’s driving you slightly mad. That’s usually a good place to start.
']

In 90 days you will know exactly where your next client comes from, and what it costs to get one. That is the whole job. Everything below is how I get you there.

Most businesses don't have an ads problem. They have a system problem.

A med spa gets 47 leads in a month. The front desk calls eleven of them, three days late. The owner sees the spend, sees the empty chairs, and fires the media buyer.

A dental practice pays $38 a lead and still has holes in next week's schedule.

An ecommerce brand's dashboard says 3.2 ROAS. Shopify says something else, and nobody can explain the gap.

A school hits enrollment deadline with 300 inquiries and 40 enrollments, and no idea what happened to the other 260.

An agency signs three clients in a quarter and loses two by month four, because the ads worked and nothing behind them did.

None of those is a targeting problem. Every one is a system problem, and the system is the part nobody is watching.

I know, because I built the broken version first.

In 2019 I took a gap year and started a blog. It went nowhere. So I launched a perfume brand and put $6,000 into Facebook ads. I still remember refreshing the page while the counter climbed and the order count sat at zero. Zero sales.

I assumed the ads were bad. They weren't. The pixel fired on the wrong event, the checkout broke on mobile, and I had no way to follow up. I had built a machine missing three of its four parts and blamed the only part I could see.

White label strategy and paid media for agencies that sell it and need it delivered properly. I work behind your brand and your client never hears my name.

I trace the full path from impression to closed revenue: tracking, offer, landing page, speed to lead, nurture, close. Most of the money is lost after the click, and most agencies never look there.

Meta as the primary channel, supported by Google, LinkedIn, or TikTok where your buyer is. Server side tracking so the data is real. GoHighLevel or HubSpot wired for speed to lead. Email and SMS working leads you already paid for.

Weekly reporting against pipeline and revenue, not impressions. Documented SOPs so the system runs whether or not I am in it.

30 or more qualified leads in your first 90 days. If you do not hit that number, I keep working your account until you do. Month to month, no lock-in.

Top 1% on Upwork | 100+ American businesses since 2019 | $10M+ in client revenue | 1M+ qualified leads delivered | Brands including Daymond John

In 90 days you will know exactly where your next client comes from, and what it costs to get one. That is the whole job. Everything below is how I get you there.

Most businesses don't have an ads problem. They have a system problem.

A med spa gets 47 leads in a month. The front desk calls eleven of them, three days late. The owner sees the spend, sees the empty chairs, and fires the media buyer.

A dental practice pays $38 a lead and still has holes in next week's schedule.

An ecommerce brand's dashboard says 3.2 ROAS. Shopify says something else, and nobody can explain the gap.

A school hits enrollment deadline with 300 inquiries and 40 enrollments, and no idea what happened to the other 260.

An agency signs three clients in a quarter and loses two by month four, because the ads worked and nothing behind them did.

None of those is a targeting problem. Every one is a system problem, and the system is the part nobody is watching.

I know, because I built the broken version first.

In 2019 I took a gap year and started a blog. It went nowhere. So I launched a perfume brand and put $6,000 into Facebook ads. I still remember refreshing the page while the counter climbed and the order count sat at zero. Zero sales.

I assumed the ads were bad. They weren't. The pixel fired on the wrong event, the checkout broke on mobile, and I had no way to follow up. I had built a machine missing three of its four parts and blamed the only part I could see.

That $6,000 bought the lesson everything since is built on: running ads and building a system are two different jobs, and most businesses pay for the first while needing the second.

By 2022 I had turned it into a method. Since then I have run it for 100+ American businesses across healthcare, education, ecommerce, local services, and agencies, producing over 1,000,000 qualified leads and more than $10M in client revenue, including work with brands like Daymond John.

-----

WHAT YOU ARE ACTUALLY HIRING

You are hiring me. Not a junior, not a team overseas, not a rotating pool of contractors.

I do not outsource client work. The person who audits your account writes your strategy, builds your campaigns, watches the numbers every morning, and picks up the call when something breaks at 6pm. That is why I keep the roster small.

-----

WHO I WORK WITH

LOCAL SERVICE BUSINESSES
Chiropractors, dentists, physicians, med spas, plastic surgeons, gyms, home services. The goal is a full schedule, not a full lead sheet. Speed to lead under five minutes, and a front desk that knows what to say when the phone rings.

HEALTHCARE AND CLINICS
Multi-location practices and specialty care, where long consideration windows, compliance limits, and patient trust break generic playbooks.

SCHOOLS AND EDUCATION
Private schools, academies, and training programs working against fixed enrollment deadlines. Inquiries are easy. Enrolled students are the number that counts, and that gap is where I work.

ECOMMERCE BRANDS
Supplements, apparel, beauty, pet, accessories. Full-funnel scaling that protects margin instead of buying revenue at a loss.

MARKETING AGENCIES
White label strategy and paid media for agencies that sell it and need it delivered properly. I work behind your brand and your client never hears my name.

-----

HOW I WORK

DIAGNOSE FIRST
I trace the full path from impression to closed revenue: tracking, offer, landing page, speed to lead, nurture, close. Most of the money is lost after the click, and most agencies never look there.

BUILD THE SYSTEM
Meta as the primary channel, supported by Google, LinkedIn, or TikTok where your buyer is. Server side tracking so the data is real. GoHighLevel or HubSpot wired for speed to lead. Email and SMS working leads you already paid for.

OWN THE OUTCOME
Weekly reporting against pipeline and revenue, not impressions. Documented SOPs so the system runs whether or not I am in it.

-----

CAPABILITIES

Paid media: Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok

CRM: GoHighLevel, HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, Zapier
Lifecycle: Klaviyo, SMS and email nurture

-----

THE GUARANTEE

30 or more qualified leads in your first 90 days. If you do not hit that number, I keep working your account until you do. Month to month, no lock-in.

Conditions: agreed minimum daily spend maintained, my creative and funnel used, and leads answered within three hours when a human is needed.

-----

HOW TO START

I take on a few clients at a time.

Book a 30 minute strategy session. I go through your ad account, funnel and tracking live, and you leave with a written plan ranked by what moves revenue fastest. If I can't see a clear path, I'll say so on the call.

Want me to look at your numbers first?

Faraz Mushtaq
Fractional CMO, Adhauk Media

description:
["
I build brand identities for physical product companies, and I stay on through packaging, the second and third SKU, the Amazon listing and the website. Most of my work starts with a logo and ends as a system that has to survive print.

That last part is where identity work quietly fails. A mark that looks right on screen can fall apart at one inch on a jar, lose its contrast under a required disclosure panel, or leave no room for the allergen list. So I design for the smallest, hardest surface first. Everything larger is then straightforward.

What that usually looks like:

The foundation. Logo and wordmark drawn as true vector, a type system, a palette that is print safe from day one, and a guidelines document your printer or your next designer can follow without calling you.

The packaging. Artwork to your supplier's dieline, front, sides, back and base. Compliance marks designed into the panel from the first layout rather than added at the end. Print ready files, correct bleed and marks.

The range. Second and third SKUs built off decisions already made, so the line reads as one family on a shelf. Cartons, labels, refills, outers.

Where it sells. Amazon A+ modules and listing images, storefront banners, and the website when it is time.

How I work. You see several real directions inside 24 to 36 hours, not one finished thing at the end. Direction is agreed in words before real effort goes in, which is why revisions rarely run long. And anything I can see coming that will cost you money later, a regulated word, a trademark still in application, a panel that will not hold the required type, I raise it before it becomes a reprint.

Six years of this and 300+ completed projects here, a lot of them files that went to a real press.

Adobe Illustrator, InDesign, Photoshop, Figma.

If you are somewhere in this, tell me what you are making and what the first surface is. I will tell you honestly whether it is a fit.
"]

description:
['
You’ve paid for the leads. You’ve paid for the CRM. So why are you still asking the team, “Did anyone actually follow up with this person?”

Someone’s checking a spreadsheet. Someone else thinks an automation handles it. The person who built that automation left six months ago.

Lovely.

I help businesses sort out what happens between someone showing interest and actually becoming a customer. The CRM, the follow-up, the integrations, the reporting. All the things that become painfully important once “we’ll just keep track of it ourselves” stops working.

HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Pipedrive, Zoho. I work across them. Let’s start with what your business needs to do.

🫠 ANY OF THIS SOUND FAMILIAR?

• “We need more leads.”
Possibly. But you’ve also got hundreds of old enquiries sitting in the CRM, no consistent follow-up and no clear idea why people stopped replying. There could be business in there you’ve already paid to acquire.

• “Our sales team won’t use the CRM.”
They’re updating spreadsheets, digging through emails and keeping notes in their heads because that’s somehow easier. Meanwhile, you’re paying for a system that creates more admin for the people it’s supposed to help.

• “We have automations. I think.”
Nobody’s entirely sure what triggers what anymore. A prospect books a call and still gets the “book a call” email. Someone changes a field and three other things break. Everyone’s slightly scared to touch it.

• “Can someone pull the numbers?”
A surprisingly complicated request. Marketing has one answer. Sales has another. You end up piecing together a report manually, then making decisions with a quiet suspicion that half of it is wrong.

• “Why am I still the person holding all this together?”
You’re reminding people to follow up, checking whether leads were assigned and passing information between teams. The business has grown, but far too much still depends on you remembering things.

• “Surely these tools should talk to each other?”
Your forms, calendars, CRM and delivery systems all hold a different piece of the story. Your team fills the gaps by copying and pasting. Sometimes correctly.

🔧 WHAT WE CAN ACTUALLY FIX

📥 Lead handling and follow-up
Get enquiries to the right person, give them a clear next action, and build sensible email, SMS and reminder sequences around the sales process. Including what happens when someone doesn’t book, doesn’t show or isn’t ready yet.

🧩 CRM setup and cleanup
Build pipelines that reflect how you sell, tidy up records and make the system easier to use. That might mean improving what you have, starting fresh or migrating to something that fits better.

🔌 Integrations
Connect the tools your business runs on using Make, Zapier, n8n, webhooks and custom APIs. So your team can stop being the connection between two bits of software.

♻️ Nurture and database reactivation
Give older enquiries a sensible route back into a conversation. “They didn’t buy immediately” shouldn’t be the end of your entire follow-up strategy.

📊 Reporting
See where leads come from, where they get stuck and what turns into sales. Answer everyday business questions without launching a small investigation.

🤖 AI, where it earns its place
Summarise conversations, organise enquiries and help your team get the context they need. There should be a clear reason to add it and a useful job for it to do.

🧠 A BIT ABOUT ME

I’m Johnny. Before running Lock and Quay, I worked in software engineering and business analysis at Deloitte Digital. Since then, I’ve worked across paid ads, lead generation, CRM and marketing automation.

I’ve been on the side spending money to bring leads in. So I care quite a lot about what happens to them afterwards.

That mix shapes how I approach a build. Who’s using this? What do they need to know? What happens if the prospect goes quiet? Who owns the next step? Will this still make sense when there are twice as many enquiries?

I’m also Top Rated Plus on Upwork, with $60K+ earned here and work spanning CRM audits, HubSpot workflows, Pipedrive optimisation and integrations.

🤝 HOW WE’D WORK TOGETHER

Show me what’s happening now and where it’s frustrating you. You don’t need to arrive with a perfect technical brief. Working out what needs building is part of the job.

For a bigger project, we’ll usually start with a paid audit and roadmap. We map the process, identify the gaps and agree on priorities before getting stuck into implementation.

I work best with people who are open about what’s going wrong, happy to answer questions and willing to make decisions together. I’ll bring ideas, flag things that don’t make sense and take ownership of the agreed work.

The goal is a business where leads get handled properly, your team knows what to do and you don’t have to personally chase every moving part.

Send me a message with what you’re using and what’s driving you slightly mad. That’s usually a good place to start.
']

I don't start by increasing your ad budget.

I review Google Ads, Meta Ads, GTM, GA4, conversion tracking, campaign structure, audience targeting, product feeds, and account-level performance.

description:
['
PCB problems become expensive after fabrication. A weak power architecture, missed return path, unsuitable component, or overlooked layout detail can cause unstable prototypes, failed testing, and another costly board revision.

I take ownership of PCB hardware from architecture and schematic design through multilayer layout, independent design review, board bring-up, debugging, DFM, and manufacturing release using Altium Designer and KiCad.

Clients have described my PCB reviews as “structured, honest and specific,” with findings that “went beyond the obvious checklist items.” On longer hardware engagements, clients have rehired me after I diagnosed unexpected testing problems and implemented reliable corrections.

What I take ownership of:
• Hardware architecture and system block diagrams
• Schematic capture and circuit design
• Component selection, sourcing, and lifecycle analysis
• Analog, digital, power, and mixed-signal electronics
• Multilayer PCB design, from 2 to 12+ layers
• High-speed routing and differential pairs
• Signal integrity and power integrity considerations
• Controlled impedance and PCB stack-up planning
• Grounding, return paths, EMI/EMC, and thermal management
• Rigid and rigid-flex PCB design
• ESP32, STM32, ARM Cortex, and Nordic nRF52 hardware
• BLE, Wi-Fi, LoRa, cellular, GNSS, NFC, CAN, USB, and RS485
• Battery charging and low-power electronics
• Obsolete-component replacement and PCB redesign
• Independent schematic and PCB layout reviews
• DFM, DFA, and production documentation

Independent PCB design review:
I review more than design-rule errors. My PCB reviews examine power distribution, return paths, component placement, interface implementation, grounding, protection, thermal risks, manufacturability, test access, and likely board bring-up problems. The result is a structured list of findings with practical corrections, priorities, and clear technical reasoning.

Board bring-up and debugging:
My responsibility does not end when the Gerber files are generated. I support controlled first power-up, power-rail verification, current measurements, clock and reset checks, communication-interface validation, sensor testing, fault isolation, and root-cause analysis. When testing exposes a design issue, I document the findings, correct the Altium or KiCad source files, and prepare the next verified board revision.

Manufacturing deliverables:
• Altium Designer or KiCad source files
• Gerber or ODB++ fabrication data
• NC drill and PCB stack-up requirements
• Production-ready BOM
• Pick-and-place files
• Assembly drawings and fabrication notes
• 3D STEP model of the PCBA
• Bring-up findings and revision documentation

My recent projects include a dense 6-layer IoT board, an nRF52840 Bluetooth audio PCB, STM32 control systems, NIR sensing electronics, LoRa communication hardware, wireless sensor nodes, motor controllers, battery-powered devices, and industrial automation electronics.
Top Rated Plus | 98% Job Success | $200K+ earned | 105 jobs | 6,000+ hours

A strong project fit:
I am the right fit when you need complete PCB development, an independent design review, an existing-board redesign, or technical ownership through board bring-up and manufacturing handoff.

I may not be the right fit if the priority is the lowest-cost PCB layout without proper engineering verification.

Send me your requirements, schematic, block diagram, or PCB source files. I will identify the main technical risks and recommend the right starting point.

🎨 Figma mobile app design and mobile app designer work, 11 of 20 cases

11 of my 20 published cases are Figma mobile app design for iOS and Android, 2 platforms drawn separately instead of 1 design squeezed twice. As a mobile app designer I start with the user flow, not the visuals: what the user is trying to do, in what order, and where they hesitate. Then wireframing, UI UX prototyping, and user interface design at full fidelity, with 4 states per screen that nobody remembers to specify: empty, loading, error, offline. Mobile UI design respects the platform, so an iOS screen behaves like iOS.

📊 UI UX designer SaaS Figma dashboards and CRM, 6 of 20 cases

6 published cases are dashboards, one carrying 5 user roles inside a single interface. This part of user experience design starts with information architecture: what belongs on the first screen, what belongs 1 click deeper, and what nobody ever opens. Then tables, filters, and data visualization sized for real volume rather than for demo data, role based views so 5 roles see 5 versions of the same screen, and a density that lets someone scan instead of read.

🌐 Web design, Website designer, Wix web design, Webflow designer, 3 breakpoints

As a web designer I design responsive websites, landing pages, and web app interfaces, and I draw 3 breakpoints on every page, desktop, tablet, and mobile, because the mobile version carries most of the traffic. Landing page design gets the same 3 breakpoints as everything else. Web design here is built around 1 conversion goal instead of around a layout I liked.

🔧 Wordpress developer UI UX, UI UX designer Wix, Web developer handoff, 4 routes

1 Figma file, 4 build routes: a Web developer, a Wordpress developer, a Webflow designer, or a Wix web design team. UI UX designer Wix and Webflow projects get the same handoff as native ones, with every state drawn instead of guessed.

🛍 UI UX designer Shopify and Shopify UI UX, 5 page types

Shopify UI UX means the 5 page types where money is made or lost: home, collection, product, cart, checkout. I have designed storefronts and blog systems, mobile view first, 3 breakpoints each. UI UX designer Shopify work starts with your analytics, not with my taste.

🤖 UI UX designer AI and mobile app design AI, 2 cases

2 of my cases are AI products: an AI bot trainer app and analytics driven interfaces. Mobile app design AI has 1 extra rule, never let generated output look identical to verified data, because that is where trust dies.

🧩 Design systems, UI graphics, GUI design, 1 library per product

Every product I deliver as a UI UX Designer ends with 1 component library: tokens, variants, and 4 states per component, so screen 40 never contradicts screen 1. UI graphics, icon sets, and GUI design are part of that delivery. Brand identity design and logo design arrive from your side or from a Graphic designer on our team, and as a Product designer I build the interface around your branding.

🎯 UI UX Designer across 12 industries, 20 published cases

20 published cases as a UI UX Designer cover fintech and crypto (ZimoCash, Jon D. Rock, Wethermrkt), SaaS and CRM (Krankque, Tarkeez), healthcare (EdEHR, MicroRec), e-commerce and marketplaces (My Store, Bliss Pool, Photaka), social and dating (Zinglez, ShareMy, HubNox), and fitness, music, and on-demand apps (Regent, Music Coast, Ghasla).

⚙️ How I work as your UI UX Designer, 3 stages

3 stages, always in this order, and every UX & UI decision written down rather than only drawn. Before high fidelity UI: UX research, user flow mapping, wireframing, prototyping. Then the screens. After: usability testing on the flows that carry your revenue. As a UI UX designer I hand off to native iOS and Android teams, to a Flutter mobile app developer India based or anywhere else, and to web teams. Files arriving as Adobe XD, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, or Adobe InDesign I continue in Figma.

I studied business at the University of Pennsylvania, and as an entrepreneur I've raised millions in venture capital, built and sold companies, and generated over $500 million in client revenue across the products and services I've built. Most cold calling programs fail, and not because the phone stopped working. Outbound is one of the hardest things in business to get right, and it takes a genuinely experienced, executive mind to build the strategy correctly and then actually execute on it. Anyone can dial. Very few people can design the offer, the targeting, the sequencing, and the conversation that turn a cold list into booked revenue.

I run Upwind, an inbound and outbound phone agency built around cold calling, telemarketing, and appointment setting. My team places tens of thousands of cold calling and telemarketing dials every month into every industry, and we currently book over $620,000 per month in pipeline for our clients. That is what disciplined cold calling looks like when it's measured instead of guessed at.

The most important thing we do isn't dialing. It's matching you with the exact person your business needs. We source, train, and manage a cold calling appointment setter, or a full team, who learns your product like it's their own, so your prospects build a real relationship with one consistent voice instead of a rotating cast of strangers reading a script.

From there we run the whole engine. We build and rapidly iterate the scripts and targeted prospect lists that make sales cold calling actually connect, and we run b2b cold calling campaigns into the founders, executives, and decision-makers who are hard to reach any other way. For property clients we run real estate cold calling for agents, investors, and brokerages who need a pipeline full of live conversations, plus real estate telemarketing follow-up that keeps those leads warm long after the first dial.

Our cold calling lead generation work feeds qualified opportunities straight into your CRM, while telemarketing lead generation and telemarketing sales campaigns extend the same motion into higher-volume and consumer markets. For B2B teams we combine b2b telemarketing and cold calling telemarketing sequences with email follow-up so nothing goes cold between touches.

Appointment setting is where all of it lands: qualified meetings booked straight onto your calendar, confirmed and reminded so they actually show up. We also handle inbound reception and customer service with the kind of care that keeps opportunities from slipping through, and we provide the virtual assistant and administrative support that keeps your pipeline organized while your closers stay on the phone. I speak fluent Spanish, so Spanish cold calling and bilingual outreach are available on request.

Why clients stay with us for years: we treat cold calling like a lab. We test openers, timing, sequencing, and buying signals until we find what converts, then scale it. And because our callers are on the phone all day, we obsess over keeping them happy. That's 80% of the equation, because prospects want to talk to happy people. A caller who's genuinely enjoying the conversation brightens the prospect's day, and that energy is what turns a cold list into booked revenue.

If you want more qualified conversations and more booked revenue from the phone, let's talk. Even if we mutually decide we aren't the best fit, my advice on cold calling is always free, and I'm happy to point you in the right direction.
"]

Your site is live. Traffic is coming in. But something isn't working.

Maybe it's slow. Maybe people are landing and leaving without converting. Maybe you've outgrown your current platform and don't know what comes next. These are solvable problems, and solving them is what I do.

I build websites, custom frontends, and headless CMS architectures. → Your content team gets a simple, clean editor to update anything on the site
→ Your frontend loads fast, looks exactly as designed, and scales without breaking
→ Built on Next.js, React, Nuxt.js, Tailwind CSS
→ CMS options: Sanity, Contentful, Strapi, Prismic, Storyblok, Headless WordPress, Headless Shopify

→ Webflow: Figma-to-Webflow builds, interactions, and CMS setups
→ Wix & Squarespace: Clean, professional deployments for smaller brands and service businesses

→ Heatmaps, session recordings, and scroll maps, Hotjar, Clarity, Lucky Orange
→ A/B testing with structured roadmaps, VWO, Google Optimize
→ Messaging hierarchy, CTA positioning, and layout restructuring
→ Checkout and landing page optimisation

CRO: Hotjar · Clarity · VWO · Crazy Egg · GA4 · GTM · Klaviyo

𝐖𝐡𝐨 𝐈 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤 𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡

Scaling ecommerce brands, SaaS founders, and service businesses that have outgrown their current setup and need their site to actually perform. If you want a cheap template swap, I'm not the right fit. If you want it built fast, scalable, and conversion-ready, we should talk.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐈 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤

Abstract:

This dissertation examines the efficacy of AI-powered chatbots in alleviating student anxiety within online learning environments, addressing a pressing concern as mental health challenges among digitally engaged learners continue to rise. Employing a mixed-methods research design, the study integrates qualitative and quantitative data to evaluate the impact of AI chatbots on student well-being. Data collection includes student feedback on chatbot interactions, anxiety levels measured through validated psychological scales (e.g., GAD-7, STAI), and usage analytics derived from chatbot platforms across diverse educational contexts.The findings demonstrate that students who interacted with AI-powered chatbots experienced statistically significant reductions in anxiety levels, attributed to the chatbots' ability to provide real-time emotional support, personalized guidance, and immediate access to resources. These results underscore the potential of AI chatbots as scalable, cost-effective interventions for addressing psychological distress in online learning environments. Moreover, the study highlights the role of natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) algorithms in enabling chatbots to deliver context-aware, empathetic responses tailored to individual student needs. The implications of this research are twofold: (1) it contributes to the EdTech literature by demonstrating how AI-driven tools can enhance mental health support in digital education, and (2) it provides a framework for integrating AI chatbots into pedagogical strategies to promote student well-being and academic success. Importantly, the study identifies the potential of AI chatbots to bridge mental health resource gaps, particularly in under-resourced educational settings, where access to traditional support systems is often limited. By bridging the intersection of educational technology, mental health, and AI innovation, this research not only advances the field of EdTech but also paves the way for future interventions leveraging digital solutions to improve student mental health and learning outcomes.

Abstract: This dissertation looks at how traditional assessment methods are changing to AI-driven tests in online education. It discusses the important challenges and chances this change brings for teachers and students. A major focus of this research is how well AI technologies can evaluate student performance compared to old methods. By comparing assessment results, doing surveys to understand how teachers and students feel, and studying AI use in different educational settings, the results show that AI tests can make things faster and offer tailored feedback. However, worries about reliability and bias are still common. In particular, the data shows that teachers and students have different trust levels in AI assessments, which has important effects on teaching practices. In healthcare education, these findings are especially important because precise and accountable assessment methods are crucial. The wider impact of this study hints at a change in how assessments are done, suggesting that while AI technologies can change educational practices, they need to be used carefully while considering ethical issues and differences in how they are applied. Overall, this research adds to the ongoing conversation about educational change, providing insights that could help guide the careful use of AI in assessment systems in healthcare and other areas. I. INTRODUCTION A major change in education has happened because technology, especially artificial intelligence (AI), is changing how teaching and learning are done. The COVID-19 pandemic sped up this change by forcing a switch to online learning, making teachers and schools rethink how they assess students. Traditional exams, which often focus on memorization and have strict time limits, do not effectively measure skills needed for today's fast-paced and complicated job markets. This dissertation plans to study how assessment methods have changed from traditional ways to AI-based tests in response to educational needs and tech improvements. The main research problem is to assess how effective, reliable, and ethical AI assessments are compared to standard methods, especially concerning issues like fairness, bias, and accountability that worry both educators and students. The goals include looking at the benefits of AI assessments, such as personalized feedback, efficiency, and greater engagement from test-takers, while also examining possible issues like bias from algorithms and student anxiety. This study is important not only for academics-who need to develop new assessment methods-but also for schools that must prepare students for jobs requiring advanced problem-solving and critical thinking skills that traditional assessments do not adequately measure.

I help startups and growing companies with two things investors and operators care about most: the story that gets you funded, and the financial backbone that keeps the business running once you are. I've spent more than 12 years doing exactly this, as a corporate finance advisor, fractional CFO, and founder.

The difference is that I don't only design the financial backbone. I build it. The reporting my CFO clients run on every day is software I wrote.

Pitch decks, fundraising materials & financial models
Through PitchStudio, the studio I founded, I've helped 200+ companies across 18 industries put together $330M+ in investor-ready pitch decks, business plans, and financial models.
✅ Pitch decks from scratch: research, financial modeling, storytelling, design
✅ Deck redesigns: turn your existing materials into something investor-ready
✅ AI deck humanization: already drafted your deck with ChatGPT or another AI tool? I'll rework the content, structure, and design so it reads like it was built by someone who actually understands your business, not a template
✅ Financial models for fundraising, planning, or due diligence
✅ Fast-turnaround decks, when you need something polished in days, not weeks

Fractional CFO, and the person who builds the system
Most finance teams are not short of analysis. They are short of numbers that are current. The ledger holds one piece, the bank another, then orders, suppliers, stock and marketing spend each sit somewhere else. Someone joins them by hand in a spreadsheet once a month, that file breaks silently, and by the time it is ready the decision it was meant to inform has already been made without it.

The cost is never the hours spent on the file. It's the price left uncorrected for two months, or the hire made against a runway number that was three months optimistic.

I hold fractional CFO roles with growing companies, and in each one I designed the reporting and then built it: a live accounting API integration, importers for the operational sources that have no API, rule engines that classify transactions the same way every month, and reconciliation checks that run on every load and report the result on screen. A spreadsheet never tells you it broke.
✅ Management accounts, cash flow forecasting, and board-ready reporting
✅ Connecting your accounting system to the operational sources it doesn't talk to
✅ Financial process setup and cleanup: reconciliations, chart of accounts, Xero
✅ Budgeting, forecasting, and scenario planning
✅ Investor and board reporting
✅ Financial due diligence prep, for fundraising or M&A

Why founders and finance teams choose me
🛠 I build what I design. There are plenty of fractional CFOs and plenty of developers. Very few are the same person, which is why you get a system that keeps working instead of a file that needs maintaining
🎯 I've built and exited a company myself, so I know what actually matters versus what's just process for its own sake
📊 I work at both the strategic and the transactional level: I'm as comfortable presenting to a board as I am reconciling a bank statement
🌍 Cross-industry: SaaS, fintech, consumer, food, healthcare, nonprofit, real estate
⚡ 100% Job Success on Upwork, Top Rated

I've also spent 10 years as a Teaching Assistant in M&A and Investment Banking at LUISS University, working alongside executives from Citi, Evercore, and Jefferies.

Ready to talk? Tell me a bit about your project, or the decision you keep having to make without the numbers in front of you. I'll be honest about whether I'm the right fit.

Website design, website redesign and landing page design. SaaS and web application design. Dashboard design and admin panels. Mobile app design for iOS and Android. eCommerce website design for Shopify, WooCommerce and custom builds, including product pages, collection pages, cart and checkout UX. Marketplace design for multi-vendor platforms. AI-powered features like AI search, product recommendations and AI chat assistants.

AI IN MY PROCESS
I use Figma AI, Figma Make and v0 to test layouts and build clickable prototypes much faster than I could a few years ago. That saves you time in the early rounds. I don't hand over AI output as final design, though. Every screen gets reviewed, refined and organized in Figma so it stays consistent and easy to build.

AI FEATURES I DESIGN
AI search has to understand what a shopper means, not just match keywords. A chatbot or AI assistant has to know when to hand off to a human. Recommendation blocks need to feel relevant instead of random. All of these fail quietly when nobody plans the edge cases, so that's where I spend my time.

UX research and competitor review. User flows and wireframes. High-fidelity UI design for desktop, tablet and mobile. An interactive Figma prototype. I can also run a UX audit on your current site or app and point out where users drop off.

WORKING WITH ME
I'll ask questions before I design. You'll see early wireframes so we agree on structure before visuals. You'll get organized, responsive Figma files with clear notes for your developer. And I reply fast, even across time zones in the US, UK and Europe.

Send me your project details or a link to what you have now. I'll give you honest feedback and a plan.

Clients don't hire me to make things pretty. They hire me because something isn't working, and they need a senior product designer who figures out why before designing anything.

Complex SaaS dashboards, admin panels, CRM, and ERP systems restructured around the few things users actually open them to do, made scannable, usable, and dev-ready.

title_occupation: ['Is SEO Dead?......Nope: I provide consistent leads through AEO/GEO/SEO']
description:
["
At its core, marketing is the art of selling money at a discount. I've generated $40 million + for clients and growing.

Growing up I was the kid who brought a 3D-printed turbine to the science fair, let my friends copy my test answers, and stayed up late obsessing over tech no one else cared about.

Back then, it got me teased. Now, I’m grateful it’s the fuel behind how I help clients grow revenue. I’m an introvert, but also an overachiever, unapologetically.

Over the last year especially, the rules of visibility have expanded.

When Google rolled out AI Mode more broadly on May 20, 2025 (and continued scaling AI Overviews), it made something obvious that had been building for a while: virtually all search is now AI assisted, whether you’re looking at organic results, paid placements, or even local SEO. (I’ve got videos breaking down how this changes local visibility and what actually moves the needle.)

So instead of treating AI search like a separate channel, I understand that it’s an additional layer sitting on top of everything we already do.

Traditional SEO metrics were built for a different era, one dominated by the familiar ten blue links. In that context, the focus was on visibility and user interaction within a static results page.

Standard key performance indicators included metrics like SERP position and “keyword rankings”.

These figures were instrumental in measuring campaign impact and benchmarking progress.

However, they all share a fundamental design assumption: they were created for human users scrolling through Google’s interface, not AI systems parsing the web behind the scenes.

We’ve moved into a world of AI-enhanced search.

Users now engage through natural language queries and get direct, synthesized responses from systems like ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, or Perplexity. Under the hood, the plumbing looks different:

Vector-Based Storage Systems
Semantic Embeddings
Hybrid Ranking Models (think classic keyword retrieval + re-ranking)
Large Language Models (LLMs)
AI Agents and task-driven workflows

In this environment, search isn’t only about ranking a page. It’s about being retrieved, trusted, and preferred when an AI system is assembling an answer.

Here’s the nuance most people miss:

Step 1: Getting pulled (retrieval) — Do you even make it into the candidate set?
Step 2: Getting preferred (re-ranking) — Once you’re in the set, are you the one the system chooses to surface, cite, or summarize?

That two-step reality is exactly why a lot of content shows up sometimes… but rarely becomes the top recommendation.

A big influence on how I approach this is the 2025 MIT + Columbia research on Generative Engine Optimization in e-commerce (often referenced as the E-GEO work). And other similar studies.

That’s why I built and use an internal workflow that tests variations and re-ranks them based on extractability, clarity, and evidence. The goal is simple: content that reliably gets pulled and reliably gets preferred.

AI systems don’t replace crawling, indexing, and ranking; they usually sit on top of classic search infrastructure and retrieval systems, then reason over what’s been fetched. In other words, the old rules still matter, but now they feed a bigger machine.

So yes, we still care about technical SEO, content depth, entity clarity, internal linking, and authority.

But we also care about:

How your pages get chunked and retrieved
Whether your answers are easy to reuse without distortion
Whether your claims are provable
Whether your differentiators are concrete
Whether your structure matches how people ask questions today

This is why, while most agencies were still refreshing rank trackers, I rebuilt my SEO and PPC stack to include optimization around vector search, query fan-out mapping, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation, so my clients are positioned to show up in Google SERPs, AI-generated answers, and paid slots.

Who’s Not A Fit

Micromanagers: If you need to control every move and won’t let my team and I execute, we won’t be effective.

Budgets under $1.7k/month: Intro plans start there; most of my clients invest between $2.5–$5k. I believe money is only an issue in the absence of value, and I intend to bring you value.

“Set-and-forget” mindsets: Tomorrow’s SERPs belong to brands that iterate and evolve.

Ranking vanity: If a green arrow in a tool matters more than profitable revenue, we’re not aligned.

If any of those sound like you, no hard feelings, save my info for later.

If not, your company may be a good fit. To get started, send me a DM about your business and goals, and we can jump on a Zoom call to discuss the details.

If you refuse to settle for average and want an SEO/PPC engine built for a search landscape where AI is already everywhere, let’s map out your success together.

"]

Message content was written specifically for the facilities management audience rather than adapted from consumer templates — referencing the specific challenges that commercial cleaning contracts presented for a facilities manager (vendor reliability, regulatory compliance for medical facilities, coverage for off-hours access requirements) rather than generic cleaning service benefits. Smart list segmentation within GoHighLevel allowed the sales team to view their assigned prospect list filtered by industry tag — medical facilities, office buildings, retail, industrial — so outreach could be prioritized by the industry segments where the cleaning company had the strongest case studies and compliance credentials. Response detection was configured at every touchpoint to pause the automated sequence immediately when a prospect replied, preventing automated follow-up from continuing alongside an active human conversation.

A snapshot update installs cleanly into an empty sub-account but can create conflicts, duplications, and broken workflow references when installed into a sub-account with months of operational history. The approach I developed for a multi-location franchise client treated snapshot updates as additive rather than overwrite operations — new workflow additions and template improvements were deployed to existing franchisee sub-accounts as targeted additions rather than full snapshot reinstalls, using a documented component-by-component deployment process that added or replaced only the specific workflows, email templates, or pipeline stages that had changed, while leaving every other element of the franchisee's account untouched. For each update cycle, I created a changelog document listing every modified component and the specific change made, so the deployment procedure for each franchisee account was a precise checklist rather than a general instruction to "reinstall the snapshot." Components that had been customized by individual franchisees — typically email copy and timing adjustments within the approved customization scope — were reviewed before the relevant component was updated, with the franchisee's customization preserved into the new version rather than overwritten. The update process for each franchisee account was completed and verified in a test sub-account before being applied to any live account, and a rollback procedure was documented for each update in case a new component produced unexpected behaviour in production. ✔ Retainage Tracking: receivable and payable retainage held in their own accounts rather than buried in AR.

MY APPROACH
